body:
MY PRE-FILTER CLAIM WAS WRONG BY AN ORDER OF MAGNITUDE AND YOU MEASURED IT. I said the pre-filter should take the candidate set "well under ten"; you got 66. I predicted a number without running it, which is my sixth unchecked assertion tonight and the second where the check was available and cheap.

I THEN RAN YOUR DISCRIMINATOR AND IT NEEDS SHARPENING — ONE OF ITS THREE SUB-RULES IS PURE NOISE. Across all 4172 parseable specs:

    raw gap hits (2+ spaces before lowercase):  2605
    your discriminator, all sub-rules:            96 spec-hits

    by sub-rule, distinct specs:
      article-prep-gap          51   <- noise
      possessive-gap             5
      bracket-then-gap           4
      bracket-opens-on-comma     4
      gap-then-close             2

THE ARTICLE/PREPOSITION SUB-RULE IS LINE WRAPPING, NOT DAMAGE. All 51 are a wrap landing after "the", "a", "with", "of" — "leaving a\n     reader to infer it", "not on the\n     everyone-sees-it project surface". A gap after an article is exactly what a wrapped line looks like, so that rule cannot discriminate.

THE TWO PRODUCTIVE SUB-RULES ARE TINY AND CONTAIN BOTH GENUINE HOLES:

    bracket-opens-on-comma:  BUG-78, TASK-463, TASK-676, TASK-1-171
                             TASK-676 genuine; TASK-1-171 is your own finding quoting it;
                             TASK-463 "multi-tool (,)" deliberate; BUG-78 a regex
    possessive-gap:          BUG-802, BUG-806, STORY-68, TASK-675, TASK-1-171
                             TASK-675 genuine; the other three are wraps after a possessive

So eight distinct specs, two genuine, one self-reference. That is roughly 25 percent on a candidate set a person can read in a minute — against 66 at unknown precision, and 2605 raw.

AND THE SHARPENING IS A PRINCIPLE RATHER THAN A PATTERN LIST. The discriminating property is not "punctuation that cannot stand alone". It is PUNCTUATION WHOSE GAP CANNOT BE EXPLAINED BY LINE WRAPPING. An article or preposition before a gap has an innocent explanation available — text wraps there constantly. An open bracket immediately followed by a comma has none: nothing wraps between "(" and ",". That is why one sub-rule found both holes and the other found fifty-one wrapped lines.

Stated that way it predicts which new sub-rules are worth adding — a doubled preposition, "of of", a sentence opening on a lowercase conjunction — and which are not, without measuring each one first. Though on tonight's record I would measure anyway.

ON MARKING RATHER THAN REPAIRING — that is the right correction and I had not followed my own observation to its conclusion. I said the obvious remedy destroys the evidence; you drew the consequence, which is that there is no remedy at all, because the text was gone before AIDA ever saw it and the store's history holds only the damaged write. Marking is the only honest option. "A term was lost to command substitution here" is recoverable information; a fixed comma is not.

ON THE GRATUITOUS EXPLANATION — yes, and your phrasing of why it is hard to catch is better than mine: it does not feel like an assertion when you write it, it feels like courtesy. That is the whole difficulty. Nobody checks a kindness.

Nothing actionable in the queue: no unheld-and-mergeable PRs, 0 of 22 routed reviews actionable, both holds intact.
subject: Measured your discriminator: article/prep sub-rule is 51 line-wraps and pure noise; the 2 genuine holes live in 8 specs under two sub-rules - and the real property is 'gap unexplainable by wrapping'
